verdict.line: You lose trades from level 1 through roughly level 10 if K'Sante lands his Q-stack shockwave into a Path Maker stun, but you win the game once your Q stacks pile up and Trinity Force comes online around level 11-15.

brief.thesis: K'Sante has two separate point-and-click engage tools (W Path Maker's charge-then-dash stun, and a Q Ntofo Strikes shockwave pull at 2 stacks) while Nasus has zero mobility or disengage of his own — this is why lane advantage and solo-kill advantage both sit with K'Sante despite the matchup landing close to even (48.9% over 1473 games) overall. Nasus doesn't out-trade that engage kit early; he out-scales it once Siphoning Strike is stacked and his core items land.

theirWindow.when: K'Sante at 2 Q stacks, W up
theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes he fires a shockwave that pulls you in, chaining straight into W (Path Maker)'s stun. Don't stand in a line with him near 2 stacks, and don't trade into him while Path Maker (14/13/12/11/10s cd) is available.

yourWindow.when: his E (Footwork) and W (Path Maker) both down
yourWindow.what: With both on cooldown he has no dash, no shield, and no stun. Step up, land Q (Siphoning Strike), drop E (Spirit Fire) under him for the armor shred, then use W (Wither) to keep him slowed in range since he can't disengage.

start.why: Measured as the top start in this matchup (49% WR over 1256 games, 70.7% pick) — the extra sustain and poke-reduction blunts K'Sante's Q line-poke while you're still behind in levels.

boots.why: Best-performing boots here (50.4% over 952 games, 56.2% pick) — the ability haste shortens your Q/W/E cooldowns so you can punish his Footwork/Path Maker downtime more often.

core.why: First item on the strongest measured path (61.9% WR over 218 games, 25.8% pick) — the damage and attack speed spike is when your trades start beating his.
The attack speed slow directly undercuts K'Sante's stacking Q (Ntofo Strikes) output, and the armor helps against his auto-attack-heavy All Out form.
Boosts Soul Eater lifesteal and all incoming healing, letting you win extended trades once he's out of cooldowns.

situational.when: he's building toward sustained auto-attack damage and you need the grievous wounds to cut his All Out healing
you need an early antiheal rush before Frozen Heart completes
you want a cheaper, earlier CC/wave-clear item instead of committing to Trinity Force first

runes.keystoneWhy: Gives you sustain and a speed burst to reposition after his Path Maker dash since Nasus has no mobility tool of his own — this is the highest-pick, best-performing page in the data (49.2% WR, 56.1% pick).

summoners.why: Highest measured win rate of the three combos run in this matchup (52.8%). Flash answers his stun/pull chain directly, and Ghost lets you close distance or disengage since you have no innate mobility to counter his dashes.

playing.title: Farm under tower early
playing.detail: From level 1 to roughly 5 he out-trades you with Q stacks into Path Maker. Use Q (Siphoning Strike) purely to stack kills on minions and avoid extended trades until your items and levels catch up.

playing.title: Never stand in his Q line at 2 stacks
playing.detail: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes he fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which chains directly into his stun. Break line of sight or side-step rather than trading face-to-face once he's at 2 stacks.

playing.title: Punish his cooldown gaps
playing.detail: W (Path Maker, 14-10s cd) and E (Footwork, 10-8s cd) are his only dash/shield/stun tools. When both are down he can't engage or escape — that's your window to step up with Q, E (Spirit Fire), and W (Wither).

playing.title: Spirit Fire before you commit
playing.detail: Drop E (Spirit Fire) on his feet or the wave to shred his armor before trading, and save W (Wither) to slow his retreat since he has no built-in speed boost outside All Out's Footwork bonus.

playing.title: Respect his ultimate at level 6+
playing.detail: R (All Out) knocks you through walls then he dashes in transformed with extra damage and healing. Cooldown starts at 120s and drops to 80s by rank 3 — don't overextend past the wave once it's up.

playing.title: Rush the 61.9% WR item path
playing.detail: Trinity Force into Frozen Heart into Spirit Visage is the strongest measured build here. Frozen Heart's attack speed slow directly blunts his stacking Q, and Spirit Visage amplifies your Soul Eater sustain.

playing.title: Look to scale, not force fights, before level 11
playing.detail: Your real power window opens once Q is stacked and Trinity Force is online, around level 11-15. Split-push and farm rather than committing to all-ins before then.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own analysis layered on top of those numbers.
